references.text: The context for John's baptismal activity: Jesus and his disciples were in Judea and baptizing, while at the same time John the Baptist continued his work ([ref:Joh 3:22|John 3:22]).
John also baptized at other places along the Jordan, as mentioned in [ref:Joh 1:28|John 1:28], where Bethany beyond the Jordan is named as a place where John baptized.

John says about his baptismal activity: "I baptize with water" ([ref:Joh 1:26|John 1:26]), which emphasizes the central role of water in his baptismal practice – consistent with the need for "much water" at Aenon.

Matthew tells about John the Baptist's work in the wilderness of Judea, where people from Jerusalem and all the region around the Jordan came to him and were baptized ([ref:Matt 3:5-6|Matthew 3:5-6]). This shows the same pattern as in John 3:23 – people came to him and were baptized.

Mark describes how John appeared in the wilderness and preached a baptism of repentance, and all Judea and everyone from Jerusalem went out to him and were baptized in the Jordan River ([ref:Mark 1:4-5|Mark 1:4-5]). The parallel "they came and were baptized" is also found in John 3:23.
In [ref:Joh 4:1-2|John 4:1-2] it is explained that Jesus (through his disciples) baptized more than John. This shows the simultaneous baptismal activity which is also the background in John 3:23.

John's disciples come to him and say that Jesus is now also baptizing and everyone is going to him ([ref:Joh 3:26|John 3:26]). This follows directly from the situation described in verse 23, where both have parallel baptismal activity.
The place where John first baptized is mentioned again in [ref:Joh 10:40|John 10:40], as a geographical reference to John the Baptist's work – connected with the places mentioned in John 3:23.
